text.tspan: A client connects: an ephemeral source port to the server's listening port
root or a capability to listen
Ephemeral (client) ports: the OS picks one
for every outgoing connection, from a fixed range
and NAT devices can run out)
A second connection from the same client gets a
different source port: that's how one browser
holds 10 connections to one website at once.
Firewalls, NAT and conntrack all track the 5-tuple.
AWS: a NACL is stateless, so it must allow the
return traffic to ephemeral ports (AWS suggests
1024–65535). Forget it and you get timeouts.
A security group is stateful and doesn't need this.
